# Semigroup generated by finitely many matrices

The semigroup generated by finitely many square matrices of the same size is the set of all their nonempty products; decision problems about it take the generators as input.

Let $M_1, \dots, M_k$ be $n \times n$ matrices with entries in a semiring, usually the integers or the rationals. The semigroup they generate is

$$
\langle M_1, \dots, M_k \rangle = \{ M_{i_1} M_{i_2} \cdots M_{i_m} : m \geq 1,\ 1 \leq i_1, \dots, i_m \leq k \},
$$

the set of all nonempty products of the generators; it need not contain the identity matrix. In the decision problems about such semigroups the generators are part of the input, given by their entries. A bound such as "for seven $3 \times 3$ matrices" fixes $k$ and $n$ and leaves only the entries of the generators, and of any further data, as input.

## Depends on

None.

## Proof depends on

None.

## Expansion

The membership, vector reachability, scalar reachability, zero-in-the-upper-left-corner and semigroup intersection problems are decision problems about such semigroups. Undecidability results for them are usually proved by encoding pairs of words as matrices and reducing the Post correspondence problem.
